name: Haiku small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Rate-sensitive small/mid-cap growth cut back to a smaller core of resilient software and cloud names, with the rate-beta legs (IWM, ARKK) trimmed and the leveraged TQQQ exposure exited, and the book held in about 63% cash while the Fed and yields are hawkish.
reassessment_note: Two things changed. First, the one dated October item I could find (Oct 8) showed surging yields and hawkish Fed commentary pushing growth equities lower, with the Nasdaq down 1.25% that day, while the Russell 2000 was flat. Second, the desk brief confirms a semiconductor-led selloff from 10-14 to 10-16 that also stopped out the TQQQ leg. Small caps are the most rate-sensitive part of this book, and IWM (-4.75%) and ARKK (-1.84%) are the largest losers. I cut IWM from 14% to 9% and ARKK from 12% to 7%, and exited TQQQ (2%, leveraged beta into a rate-led selloff). I kept SHOP, DDOG, UPST, SNOW (2%), CRWD (trimmed from 5% to 4%) and MDB (1%) at or near current size, and raised cash to 63%. Caveat: search returned almost nothing dated October 2026, so I could not confirm the October marks or any company news for these names. This decision rests on the packet marks plus the rate and semiconductor backdrop above, and the cash level is a hedge against a rate shock I could not size precisely.

positions.thesis: Kept a smaller Russell 2000 core for small-cap exposure. Cut from 14% to 9% because small caps are the most sensitive to hawkish-Fed and rising-yield moves, and IWM is the largest drawdown in the book (-4.75%). Stop at 12% keeps a defined loss if the rate selloff deepens.

Kept a reduced innovation-growth sleeve. Cut from 12% to 7% because ARKK is high-beta to real yields and has outflows, and it is down 1.84%. A smaller position keeps exposure to a rebound in unprofitable growth without carrying the full rate risk.

Held the strongest winner (+30.44% on the leg, mark 169.52). Kept at 5% rather than added, since the stock has run hard and the London line data I found is not a reliable U.S. quote. The 12% stop protects the gain, and the 40% take-profit caps it.

Held a small position in the observability software name that is in the green (+7.07%). Search results indicate sector strength in 2026, though I found no October news. Kept at 4% for exposure to cloud infrastructure demand without adding to rate risk.

Held the AI-lending name at 5% with its existing 35% take-profit and 12% stop. Its leg is -5.19%, but the position is small and the stop bounds the loss. Position size is kept, not raised, because it is a rate-sensitive credit name.

Held the data-cloud name at its existing 2% size (-7.30% on the leg, mark 306.84). Search indicated the stock was well off its highs with compressed multiples, which is a partial case for holding. Not raised, since the leg is losing. The 12% stop and 25% take-profit bound the outcome.

Trimmed from 5% to 4% in the cybersecurity software name, which is -5.79% on the leg and was in the semiconductor-led selloff pattern of 10-16 (the sister book was stopped out there). Kept a small core position with a 12% stop rather than a full exit, since security demand is steadier than rate-sensitive growth.
Kept the minimal 1% database position at -10.30% on the leg. Too small to matter much either way, so I kept it as a token position rather than adding. The 12% stop bounds it.
